title: A2: Handle everyday life with growing independence
outcome: Understand and take part in short connected exchanges about familiar life in Canada; recount simple events, describe routines and places, explain a problem, make plans, and complete progressively scaffolded TCF Canada tasks in listening, reading, writing and speaking.

planned_focused_hours_per_unit.note: Pacing estimate, not a completion rule. Move on when delayed recall and a new-context task show usable mastery.

study_design.learner_context: Adult learners in Canada using ParleSprint on an iPad beside a notes app.
principles: Start with a meaningful Canadian-life scene; make the French understandable with audio, context and brief English support.
Use adult strengths: concise grammar explanations and learner notes, followed immediately by French comprehension and production.
Make notes active: learner records a pattern, an original example and one error, then closes the notes and retrieves the language.
Use goal-bound tutor conversations with a hint ladder, selective correction and a second attempt in a changed situation.
Review vocabulary and grammar after delays and in new scenes; track recognition and independent production separately.
Every unit includes listening, reading, speaking, writing, and a transfer task that is not a memorized dialogue.
TCF practice follows official task types and is tracked separately from everyday conversational transfer. No score guarantees.
study_design.review_gap_note: Starting schedule for adaptive retrieval practice, not a claim that one interval sequence is optimal for every learner. Bring an item back sooner when retrieval fails.

research_basis.source: Kim and Webb (2022), The Effects of Spaced Practice on Second Language Learning: A Meta-Analysis, Language Learning 72(1), 269–319.
research_basis.finding: Across 48 experiments and 3,411 participants, spaced practice had a medium-to-large average effect on second-language learning; longer spacing outperformed shorter spacing on delayed tests, while equal and expanding schedules were statistically equivalent.
research_basis.course_application: Use delayed retrieval and adapt the next review to whether the learner recalls the item. The proposed day gaps are a practical starting schedule, not an individually proven optimum.

research_basis.source: Li, Wang and Yang (2025), Can Generative AI Chatbots Promote Second Language Acquisition? A Meta-Analysis, Journal of Computer Assisted Learning 41(4), e70060.
research_basis.finding: The review synthesized 41 experimental or quasi-experimental studies, 48 effect sizes and 3,515 participants, reporting a positive average effect (ES 0.576).
research_basis.course_application: Use Marie for objective-bound practice and feedback, then check performance in a changed situation. This broad L2 result is not evidence that this app makes French learning faster or guarantees TCF results.

unit_template.title: Words in a scene
unit_template.note: Five contextual word groups; teach only useful, high-frequency items and recycle A1 vocabulary.

unit_template.title: Chunks and retrieval
unit_template.note: Useful spoken blocks, then recall them without looking and adapt them to the learner's life.

unit_template.title: Grammar for the task
unit_template.note: One main pattern at a time: plain-English explanation, notice it in context, guided use, independent example.

unit_template.title: Goal-bound interaction
unit_template.note: Two original Canadian scenes; include clarification, follow-up and repair, not just scripted turn-taking.

unit_template.title: Connected reading
unit_template.note: One original story that recycles current and prior language; use it for meaning and retelling.

unit_template.title: Listen for meaning
unit_template.note: Short connected speech; one-play exam-style questions plus an independent gist/detail retell.

unit_template.title: Read real-world formats
unit_template.note: Original messages, notices, schedules or short information texts; teach scanning and inference.

unit_template.title: Write, check, rewrite
unit_template.note: Supported output first, then a TCF-aligned task with a checklist and a later independent retry.

unit_template.title: Speak, repair, transfer
unit_template.note: Marie follows a fixed objective, offers graduated hints, gives selective feedback and changes the scenario for the retry.

unit_template.title: TCF practice and mastery gate
unit_template.note: Cumulative retrieval, four-skill check and an unfamiliar transfer prompt; weak items feed later reviews.

units.title: A week in my life: connect the details
units.situation: A learner explains a busy week to a coworker or classmate and asks follow-up questions.
units.can_do: Connect several short present-tense ideas, give a simple reason or contrast, ask someone to clarify, and write a short connected message.
units.canada_context: An adult learner balances work, French class, transit and appointments in a Canadian city; notes are made beside the lesson on an iPad.
canada_vs_france: Use clear standard French for production; mark only verified Canadian vocabulary differences.
units.learning_loop: Attempt the scene before reading its translation; record one pattern and one personal example; retrieve them with notes closed the next day; use the same language in a different conversation later in the unit.
units.transfer_check: Explain a different week from a new prompt without using the unit's model sentences.

tcf_corner.listening: Short connected message: identify schedule, reason and one detail.
tcf_corner.reading: Read a short message or timetable and distinguish main point from details.
tcf_corner.speaking: Directed interview: describe a week and answer two unannounced follow-up questions.
tcf_corner.writing: Scaffold a 60–80 word message, building toward the TCF Task 1 range of 60–120 words.

units.title: What happened this week?
units.situation: Tell a friend or colleague about completed errands, classes and events.
units.can_do: Describe completed everyday actions in the recent past and understand their order in a short message.
units.canada_context: A learner recounts a week involving a clinic, library, grocery store, transit and French class.
units.learning_loop: Retrieve A1 time expressions, notice the past form in a short story, practise from meaning to French, then recount a different day after a delay.
units.transfer_check: Give a 45-second account of a new set of events without seeing a model.

tcf_corner.listening: Identify when and what happened in one-play messages.
tcf_corner.speaking: Task 1 interview: describe a recent activity and answer follow-ups.
tcf_corner.writing: Write a 60–90 word message recounting an event with time order.

units.title: Everyday events: what I did
units.situation: Tell a classmate about completed errands, classes and first experiences in Canada.
units.can_do: Describe completed familiar actions with several common irregular past forms and place events in a clear order.
units.canada_context: A learner recounts completed events from a week involving a clinic, library, grocery store, transit and French class.
units.learning_loop: Retrieve the regular past forms from Unit 2, notice fait, pris, vu, lu and eu in a short listening scene, then recount a different day after a delay.
units.transfer_check: Give a 45-second account of a new day using at least two taught irregular past forms, without seeing a model.

tcf_corner.listening: Identify what happened and put completed events in order.
tcf_corner.speaking: Describe a recent activity and answer follow-up questions.
tcf_corner.writing: Write a 60–90 word message recounting an event with time order.

units.title: Tell a clear story
units.situation: Explain what was happening when a plan changed or a problem occurred.
units.can_do: Use past-event forms to make a simple story understandable, with a background, event and outcome.
units.canada_context: A delayed bus, weather change or appointment mix-up gives a realistic reason to narrate and resolve a problem.
units.learning_loop: Notice how imparfait sets a past routine or scene; then contrast it with the completed-event forms from Units 2 and 3. Retell a different event after a delay.
units.transfer_check: Explain a new interruption and its result without copying the lesson story.

tcf_corner.reading: Follow a short narrative with two time frames.
tcf_corner.speaking: Tell a brief connected story and answer a why-question.
tcf_corner.writing: Write a short account with a beginning, event and result.

units.title: Work, study and future plans
units.situation: Discuss a course schedule, a work change and plans for next month.
units.can_do: Talk about near plans and simple future intentions, and understand dates and conditions in a schedule.
units.canada_context: A learner plans a class, a shift and an appointment around transit and work responsibilities.
units.learning_loop: Predict from a schedule, compare two future forms in context, then plan a different week and retrieve the forms after a delay.
units.transfer_check: Explain a plan that changes because of a new schedule.

tcf_corner.listening: Understand a schedule change and future intention.
tcf_corner.reading: Scan a short course or work notice for dates and requirements.
tcf_corner.speaking: Explain a plan and give one reason.
tcf_corner.writing: Write a short message about an upcoming change.

units.title: Choose a home and describe a neighbourhood
units.situation: Compare rental options and ask questions about a neighbourhood.
units.can_do: Compare two familiar places and combine information into clearer descriptions.
units.canada_context: Read original rental notices and discuss transit, heating, laundry and access to services in a Canadian city.
canada_vs_france: Use verified Canadian rental terms only; explain regional terms rather than presenting them as universal French.
units.learning_loop: Compare two notices, mark one useful pattern in notes, use it in a simulated conversation, and later compare unseen options.
units.transfer_check: Recommend one of two new apartments and explain the choice with two details.

tcf_corner.listening: Compare two housing options from spoken details.
tcf_corner.reading: Read a rental notice and infer which option fits stated needs.
tcf_corner.speaking: Ask a landlord several relevant questions.
tcf_corner.writing: Write a short inquiry about an apartment.

units.title: Health, appointments and getting help
units.situation: Describe a concern, ask for help and follow appointment instructions.
units.can_do: Explain a simple health or service problem and refer to a thing already mentioned.
units.canada_context: Clinic, pharmacy, 811 and 911 contexts are clearly distinguished; emergency guidance is factual and not presented as medical diagnosis.
canada_vs_france: Canadian health-system terms are checked against Government of Canada terminology sources.
units.learning_loop: Practise listening to instructions before reading them, then role-play a new request with Marie and retrieve the object-pronoun pattern later.
units.transfer_check: Explain a different appointment issue and ask for the missing information.

tcf_corner.listening: Identify instructions, time and next step.
tcf_corner.reading: Read an appointment notice and locate required information.
tcf_corner.speaking: Role-play a clinic or pharmacy interaction.
tcf_corner.writing: Write a short message to confirm or change an appointment.

units.title: Ask, answer and follow up at work or school
units.situation: Exchange detailed practical information with a colleague, instructor or classmate.
units.can_do: Ask who receives an action, give someone information, and keep a short exchange going.
units.canada_context: An adult learner asks for clarification about a work shift, class assignment or service appointment.
units.learning_loop: Use information-gap tasks so each person has a reason to ask; notes capture the form, not the whole dialogue; repeat with changed names and details.
units.transfer_check: Get three missing details from a new role-play without a prepared question list.

tcf_corner.listening: Track who gives or receives which information.
tcf_corner.reading: Understand a short work or school message.
tcf_corner.speaking: Ask follow-up questions in a guided interaction.
tcf_corner.writing: Write a clear practical message to a colleague or classmate.

units.title: Travel across the city and beyond
units.situation: Navigate a trip, ask for directions and explain a travel change.
units.can_do: Refer to places without repeating every place name and describe a simple trip or change.
units.canada_context: Use original examples from city transit, intercity buses and trains; route details must be invented or verified, never presented as current schedules.
units.learning_loop: Listen to an announcement for the destination, use a map or route diagram, then explain a new route without looking at the model.
units.transfer_check: Adapt a journey when a new service interruption is announced.

tcf_corner.listening: Identify destination, platform or route change.
tcf_corner.reading: Scan a schedule-style notice for the relevant trip detail.
tcf_corner.speaking: Ask for and confirm directions in a role-play.
tcf_corner.writing: Send a short message explaining a delay and a revised arrival plan.

units.title: Food, shopping and quantities
units.situation: Compare options, buy the right quantity and explain a preference.
units.can_do: Talk about quantities without repeating the whole noun and compare familiar choices.
units.canada_context: Shopping vocabulary is clear across Canada; Québec-specific everyday words are marked as regional when appropriate.
canada_vs_france: Keep formal production standard and label regional forms as regional.
units.learning_loop: Rebuild a shopping list from memory, listen to a changed order, then use quantities in a new menu or shopping situation.
units.transfer_check: Choose between two unfamiliar baskets and justify the quantity and value.

tcf_corner.listening: Track items, quantity and price in a short order.
tcf_corner.reading: Read a menu, flyer or return notice for specific information.
tcf_corner.speaking: Ask for a quantity and explain a preference.
tcf_corner.writing: Write a short message about a meal or purchase.

units.title: Solve a practical problem politely
units.situation: Explain a service problem, give or follow simple instructions, and make a polite request.
units.can_do: Ask someone to take a practical action politely, give a simple instruction and explain what needs to change.
units.canada_context: Original scenarios include a billing question, a missed delivery, a landlord repair request and a government-office information request; no legal advice is given.
canada_vs_france: Practise vous for unfamiliar service contacts and tu only when the relationship makes it appropriate.
units.learning_loop: First attempt the request, use a concise correction, rewrite it in notes, then handle a different service problem without the sample.
units.transfer_check: Make a polite request in an unfamiliar service scenario and confirm the next step.

tcf_corner.listening: Understand a procedure and the next action.
tcf_corner.reading: Read a service notice and identify what the reader must do.
tcf_corner.speaking: Role-play a polite request and follow-up.
tcf_corner.writing: Write a clear short service message with the problem, request and contact details.

units.title: A2 capstone: handle a changing week
units.situation: Combine plans, past events and practical requests across work, study, health and transit.
units.can_do: Understand the main point and relevant details in short connected texts, manage a routine interaction, tell a simple story and write a clear practical message.
units.canada_context: A multi-day scenario requires listening, reading, speaking and writing without relying on one rehearsed script.
units.learning_loop: Use cumulative retrieval before review, then repeat the capstone with changed names, dates, places and a new problem after a delay.
units.transfer_check: Complete a new four-skill scenario, with receptive and productive results reported separately.

tcf_corner.listening: Section-length practice with varied A2-level original items.
tcf_corner.reading: Section-length practice with original everyday texts.
tcf_corner.speaking: Short directed interview, practical interaction and supported first opinion task.
tcf_corner.writing: Complete all three task shapes progressively; Task 2 and Task 3 remain supported previews, not A2 mastery claims.
